 bleed_attack_bonus : The Bleed Attack Bonus (abbreviated as Bleed BNS in-game) increases the amount of Bleed buildup inflicted per hit. It does not affect the total amount of damage the Bleed effect will do. Unlike weapons that have a magical scaling stat, Bleed has no equivalent scaling.

The Bleed BNS value is determined by the Dexterity and Faith stats. In order to continually increase innate Bleed BNS, both Dexterity and Faith need to be leveled up, with Dexterity giving a larger bonus.

 infusion : Steady Hand McDuff can infuse most weapons with Bleed through the use of a Bleed Stone. Once a weapon is infused, the Bleed icon () will be displayed next to its image in the HUD.

Uninfused weapons imbued with Bleed gain a fixed Bleed buildup value (which does **not** scale with the Bleed Attack Bonus), but the base physical damage is lowered by 30%. For example, if a regular weapon that deals 100 physical damage is infused with Bleed, its stats switch over to 70 physical damage and 112 Bleed buildup.
Weapons with innate Bleed buildup gain an additional increase to Bleed buildup, but the base physical damage is lowered by 5%, as is the current scaling. For example, the Bandit's Knife goes from 65 physical damage + 67 Bleed buildup to 62 physical damage + 96 Bleed buildup when infused.
Shields gain additional Bleed resistance while lowering other resistances.

 bleed_buildup : When attacked with weapons that inflict Bleed, the target's Bleed meter gradually fills. The rate at which this fills is dependent on the Bleed buildup value of the attacker's weapon or item; and the target's Bleed Resist stat. The Bleed meter will gradually reset back to zero naturally, provided additional Bleed attacks are not endured.

Once the meter is full, the target's Health will damaged by 200 points. It will also reduce the maximum stamina of the target to 75% for 5 to 10 seconds. Also any movements that are not a run, dash or roll are reduced to a walk.

Its not possible to increase the total amount of damage Bleed inflicts - only the rate at which Bleed builds up can be increased. Depending on the source, the Bleed buildup value can vary greatly.

snippet:
Corvian Knight -  Dark Souls III - enemy - description 
 description : Corvian Knights are tall avian warriors that tower over their lesser brethren and are considerably more intelligent and fearsome. They exist in two variations, one that wears a hooded robe and wields the Crow Quills, and a naked variant that wields the Crow Talons.

They can be encountered throughout the Corvian Settlement exterminating other Forlorn Corvians, although they will quickly turn their attention to the player.

title: Corvian Knight
snippet:
Corvian Knight -  Dark Souls III - enemy - lore 
 lore : Corvian Knights presumably protected the Corvian Settlement and its inhabitants within the Painted World of Ariandel. Whenever a Painting begins to rot, those who settled within it resolve to burn it away in order to give way for the creation of a new one. When the Corvians were faced with this event, they were prepared to burn it. However, after Sister Friede arrived in the Painting, the Corvian Knights became infatuated with her, choosing to loyally serve her and assist in her mission to let the world rot instead. To that end, the Corvian Knights betrayed their brethren, and their loyalty to Friede was so devout that they willingly slaughtered their own kin if they were perceived to be a threat.

title: Corvian Knight
snippet:
Corvian Knight -  Dark Souls III - enemy - strategy 
 strategy : Corvian Knights are incredibly agile opponents and will regularly backflip away or leap over the player to disorient them, often following up with a lunging stab. This can be punished by dodging and backstabbing. Their flurry of blade attacks can rapidly inflict bleed, even when guarding through a shield, so it's not recommended to attempt to block their strikes. From a distance, they will throw several knives and will often perform this attack if the player attempts to heal or use an item.

The robed Corvian Knights will pursue and eliminate the lesser Corvians around the settlement, although they will focus on the player if alerted. The variant wielding talons is often encountered hiding upside down under bridges and ceilings, so it is advisable for the player to be mindful of their surroundings.

 lead : The **Deprived** is one of the classes in *Dark Souls 2*.

Unlike the other classes, it doesn't start with any weapons or Lifegems and only has the unequipped Imported Set as armor. Make sure to retrieve the Dagger found in the first side path of Things Betwixt as an initial weapon, while the Morning Star in Majula can be wielded two-handed with 2 more Strength and 1 more Dexterity. A Cleric's Sacred Chime can be found near the Morning Star if wanting to use Miracles, a Shield can be gained by either buying one of Maughlin the Armorer in Majula or be found on the path to Heide's Tower of Flame, and a Sorcerer's Staff can be found behind a hidden wall in the Forest of Fallen Giants.

The low level means leveling up is slightly cheaper than for any other class, and the all-6 statline serves as a decent base for a build focused on the Mundane infusion since that scales of the lowest stat.

 strategy : Due to the hindered movement in deep water, it is strongly advised to fight these enemies on dry land, as the reduced mobility makes evading their attacks much tougher. One should try and lure it onto one of the "islands" that have fires burning on them.

Whilst the dark projectiles cause little damage individually, they can be potentially fatal if the player has been injured by a melee attack, and also cause a brief stun effect.

Surprisingly fast despite their size, Elder Ghrus do have difficulty turning, so if the player stands behind them, they can avoid most of their attacks, although the projectiles are still a threat.

Ranged weapons can be used to lure Elder Ghrus away from other enemies, and this is strongly advised if the player wishes to obtain the Pharis's Hat and Black Bow, as they must defeat three of these beasts to receive the items.

In order to continually increase innate Fire Attack Bonus, either Intelligence, Faith, or both need to be leveled up.

The cap for Fire Bonus is affected by the total number of points in Intelligence and Faith. This means that a player with 50 Intelligence and 10 Faith will have the same Fire Bonus as one with 10 Intelligence and 50 Faith or one with 30 in both, as they all have 60 total points.

title: Parameter Bonus
snippet:
Parameter Bonus -  Dark Souls - mechanic - stat_rating 
 stat_rating : The stats that improve damage aren't directly used in the calculations; instead, they are first converted to a *rating,* which increases very quickly at low stat levels but slows down after reaching certain "soft caps." All attributes use the same conversion table to determine the bonus they receive from scaling, and Humanity uses its own.

Between each of the data points in the conversion tables, scaling increases linearly. Standard, raw, and crystal weapons, as well as weapons upgraded with twinkling titanite, demon titanite, or dragon scales, use the first table for determining the bonus damage from attributes. Weapons ascended down the Magic, Enchanted, Divine, and Occult paths use the second table for determining bonus damage from attributes.

* *Upgrade Block* is applied while using the new *Base Block*.

Giant Warrior Club -  Dark Souls II - weapon - characteristics 
 characteristics : Fully upgraded, the Giant Warrior Club ties with the Malformed Skull for the weapon with the highest physical attack rating in *Dark Souls II*, reaching a maximum of 520 damage. Ultimately, the Warrior Club hits harder than the Malformed Skull, as the former has an A scaling in Strength, whereas the latter has no attribute scaling bonuses. The base damage of the Giant Warrior Club can be further increased through a Raw infusion, to reach a maximum of 598 damage, but severely lowering the Strength scaling bonus to D.

The weapon also has the highest Strength requirement in the base game to wield one-handed, at 60 Strength. However, the Smelter Hammer from the DLC is higher, at 70 Strength. It is also the second heaviest weapon by a margin of 5 units, being outweighed by the Smelter Hammer.

The Giant Warrior Club uses regular Titanite to upgrade.

title: Deprived (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Deprived (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - lead 
 lead : The **Deprived** is one of the classes in *Dark Souls 3*.

It has a complete lack of focus in its stats, with all of them being 10 at the start. In combination with its low level of 1 this makes it a flexible, if non-optimal base for any build or respec the player wishes to do.

The Club is a simple yet strong weapon thanks to its quick attack speed and good strike damage. Its Weapon Art, Warcry, further increases damage by 10% for 30 seconds, and replaces the jump of its heavy attack with a flurry of blows, turning it into a stronger yet similarly niche attack. Its main disadvantage is its heavy focus on Strength-scaling as that might limit build potential a bit.

title: Astora Straight Sword
snippet:
Astora Straight Sword -  Dark Souls III - weapon - characteristics 
 characteristics : Although it has a minimum requirement in Faith in order to be used effectively, the Astora Straight Sword does not scale with Faith (unless it is infused down the Blessed/Lightning path), nor is it innately-blessed (unlike Anri's Straight Sword).

While it does have higher base damage than the Long Sword, it should be noted that it scales worse in Dexterity, and continues to scale unremarkably with both Strength and Dexterity, even at maximum reinforcement, and when it is made into a refined weapon.

Unlike its *Dark Souls* variant, it does not have magic damage or blessed damage.

title: Greatsword (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Greatsword (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - weapon - characteristics 
 characteristics : The Greatsword is an extreme ultra greatsword, giving up versatility and efficiency for sheer size and raw power. Its overhead swings reach high above the wielder, and its horizontal attacks cover a large area in front of the wielder. The Greatsword also features a low Dexterity requirement of 10 and the highest potential attack rating of all Heavy-infused ultra greatswords, lending itself well to strength builds looking to overpower their enemies. Its high base damage also lends itself well to the non-scaling Deep and Fire infusions, although Raw is always outperformed by Heavy.

However, it is the third heaviest ultra greatsword in the game at 20 weight units, and its two-handed attacks can be difficult to use against nimble opponents, as the vertical nature of the light attacks make them relatively easy to avoid.

title: Thief (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Thief (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - lead 
 lead : The **Thief** is one of the classes in *Dark Souls 3*.

It is a class focused on Dexterity and Luck, making it good for a build focused on light or status inflicting weapons, such as the Scimitar or the Uchigatana, or weapons with the Sharp, Blood, or Hollow Infusions. It also has just enough Attunement and Intelligence to immediately use supportive Sorceries such as Spook for increased stealth or Magic Weapon for extra damage without additional investment in those stats.

title: Lothric War Banner
snippet:
Lothric War Banner -  Dark Souls III - weapon - characteristics 
 characteristics : As a pike, the Lothric War Banner does not have any major defining characteristics with regards to its moveset aside from having a spear's running attack instead of the normal charge of the pikes.

Statistically, it is quite strong for melee-focused builds, as it can reach A scaling in either Strength or Dexterity through Heavy or Sharp infusion respectively, or have B scaling in both through Refined infusion.

It is shorter than other pikes by a very small amount, still having very good reach. In exchange for this near-nonexistent drawback, it is much lighter than other weapons in its category, with the rest being at least 50% heavier.

title: Parameter Bonus (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Parameter Bonus (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - overview 
 overview : As a rule of thumb, a weapon's physical damage is affected by the wielder's Strength and Dexterity, while elemental damage is affected by Intelligence and/or Faith. Some weapons, such as Anri's Straight Sword and Hollow weapons, also scale with Luck.

However, there are also some exceptions, such as the Saint Bident and Blessed weapons, which scale their physical damage with Faith, as well as Strength and Dexterity.

How effectively a weapon scales is not only affected by the weapon's parameter bonus, but also its base damage. As such, weapons with high scaling but low base damage are likely to get less bonus damage than a weapon with more base damage and similar scaling. It is even possible that a weapon with a considerably worse parameter bonus gets more scaling due to having much higher base damage.

title: Palestone
snippet:
Palestone -  Dark Souls II - item - description 
 description : This upgrade material will remove an infusion from any weapon. To use it, the player must first give McDuff the Dull Ember and select the "Infuse weapon" option when speaking to him. A Palestone does not need to be used in order to change infusions.

title: Broadsword (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Broadsword (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - weapon - characteristics 
 characteristics : The Broadsword is a short sword with a wide blade that emphasizes slashing, and thus, offers no thrust attacks. In turn, the Broadsword features high base damage and good strength scaling, allowing the sword to deal formidable damage at any point in the game. Additionally, the broad slash attacks allow the sword to dispatch groups of enemies with ease. However, care should be taken when in tight corridors or near walls, as the sword is likely to bounce off of solid objects, rendering the wielder vulnerable for a brief moment.

title: Parameter Bonus (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Parameter Bonus (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - lead 
 lead : The **Parameter Bonus**, also known as **Scaling**, is a mechanic in *Dark Souls III*. It indicates the level of bonus damage one can do with a weapon, based on the associated stats. In order of most to least effective, this rating can be S, A, B, C, D or E.

title: Winged Knight Halberd
snippet:
Winged Knight Halberd -  Dark Souls III - weapon - characteristics 
 characteristics : The Winged Knight Halberd is a Strength-oriented halberd whose moveset is composed entirely of wide swinging attacks. It requires copious amounts of Strength in order to wield effectively, and scales primarily with that stat. Its high base damage makes it particularly strong with non-scaling infusions, but it works best when infused with a Heavy Gem.

Like all other halberds, it deals the most damage when it hits enemies with the blade rather than the shaft. However, it also lacks the thrust attacks that the standard Halberd possesses, limiting its effectiveness against enemies weak to Thrust damage and in combat in narrow corridors.

title: Raw (upgrade path)
snippet:
Raw (upgrade path) -  Dark Souls - mechanic - overview 
 overview : Raw increases the base damage of a weapon, while reducing its stat scaling from Strength and Dexterity. As its name suggests, it gives the weapon jagged edges, making it more dangerous but also more unwieldy.

It is a unique upgrade path in that it does not allow a second tier of ascension. It essentially functions as a way for players to maximize their attack power early on in the game, with Raw +5 weapons generally more powerful than Normal +10 weapons. However, Normal +15 weapons are always stronger than their Raw +5 counterparts.

title: Flamberge (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Flamberge (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - weapon - characteristics 
 characteristics : Despite having an average moveset, the Flamberge excels in its raw damage, while also being the only greatsword to inflict bleed and dealing purely Slash damage (with exception of the Stance strong attack, which deals Thrust damage).

This raw damage does have the penalty of a very poor scaling, but it is still very good, and its minimal requirements to wield it properly might make it an attractive choice for any player.

title: Moonlight Greatsword (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Moonlight Greatsword (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - weapon - characteristics 
 characteristics : A time-honored classic returning from the previous *Souls* games, the Moonlight Greatsword is a strong weapon in the hands of a dedicated Sorcery caster.

Unlike its previous iterations, *Dark Souls III*'s Moonlight Greatsword inflicts both physical and Magic damage, as well as being given scaling in Strength, albeit poorly. However, this does not change the fact that the physical scaling should be ignored, outside of meeting the minimum wielding requirements, in favor of leveling Intelligence, as the Moonlight Greatsword has been traditionally built (though as is the case with most melee weapons, it only scales effectively up to 40 in the offensive stats). The physical damage component is useful when performing criticals, as both damage types are magnified during the attack, allowing it to more easily punch through foes' flat Defenses.

title: Club (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Club (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - weapon - characteristics 
 characteristics : The Club is a fast and hard-hitting weapon. This, combined with its relatively low weight and requirements, makes it a formidable weapon that is easily overlooked.

The main weakness of the Club is its heavy attacks, which are slow and heavily telegraphed, especially in comparison to the light attacks. However, these attacks will also hit much harder than the average heavy attack.

The Warcry skill will further increase the Club's damage output, as well as change the normal heavy attack to a four-hit combo. This attack is harder to hit and is far more punishing, should it miss, but it also deals exceptional damage should all four hits connect.

title: Painting Guardian's Curved Sword
snippet:
Painting Guardian's Curved Sword -  Dark Souls III - weapon - trivia 
 trivia : When infused, the "Curved" part of the sword's name will be replaced with whatever infusion is applied. For example, a raw infusion will rename it to "Painting Guardian's Raw Sword."
**Additionally, some infusions, such as lightning, will exclude the "Sword", instead showing up as "Painting Guardian's Lightning", from the name when viewing a reinforced variant through Andre's reinforcement or infusion menu.

title: Follower Javelin
snippet:
Follower Javelin -  Dark Souls III - weapon - characteristics 
 characteristics : The Follower Javelin is almost identical to the Spear in most regards, but it is notably different in its weapon art. The Javelin's weapon art has the player throw an illusory spear that will deal the same amount of damage as the light attack would. This has a surprisingly large range which can be incredibly useful for players that want to have a ranged form of attack but do not want to switch to a bow or crossbow in the middle of combat, or do not want to use spells.

It also has good scaling with Strength (having A scaling when fully upgraded and infused with Heavy) and has very low weight.

Its main drawback is that it is the second shortest spear in the game, only beating the Golden Ritual Spear.

The magnificent sharp curved blade instils fear in opponents. Perhaps it is their survival instinct at work.

title: Deep Gem
snippet:
Deep Gem -  Dark Souls III - item - usage 
 usage : In order to unlock the Deep infusion for use, the player must first give the Sage's Coal to Blacksmith Andre.

Using a Deep Gem will infuse the target weapon with a deepened form of Dark, and in turn, will make a weapon deal both physical damage and dark damage, at an equal-split margin with one another.

Deep infusions also remove *all* scaling effects present on the weapon after infusion, much like a Fire Gem does, which means in order to achieve maximum damage on deep weapons, the player will have to fully-reinforce one.

title: Medium Armor Sets (Dark Souls II)
snippet:
Medium Armor Sets (Dark Souls II) -  Dark Souls II - armor - characteristics 
 characteristics : In comparison to Light Armor, the Medium Armor sets are heavier (and therefore slower), but much lighter than the Heavy Armor sets (therefore faster during combat), and this will play a large role in how you play the game, ranging from PvE and PvP.

It is recommended that new players start out with mostly Medium Armor Sets, and they can make a decision for themselves. If they find they are taking too much damage, then they can make the choice to switch to a Heavy Armor Set, and if they feel like they are too slow, or they take too little damage for the defensive properties to be worth the weight, they may choose to choose a Light Armor Set.

title: Mail Breaker (Dark Souls II)
snippet:
Mail Breaker (Dark Souls II) -  Dark Souls II - weapon - characteristics 
 characteristics : Strong attacks with this weapon completely bypass shield defenses.

Due to its low base damage and mediocre scaling, it is wise to infuse with either bleed, poison, or mundane.

This is a niche weapon, as it works great against tanks and greatshield users, especially when infused with bleed or poison.

title: Standard (Dark Souls II upgrade path)
snippet:
Standard (Dark Souls II upgrade path) -  Dark Souls II - mechanic - lead 
 lead : **Standard** Reinforcement is a basic form of improving weapons and armor in *Dark Souls II*, that also appeared in *Dark Souls* beforehand. It is independent of the other infusions unlike in *Dark Souls*; you can reinforce an infused weapon, and a reinforced base weapon will not lose its levels from infusion. Also, in contrast to *Dark Souls*, common equipment can be reinforced only up to +10, not +15.
